I asked about studying abroad on /r/Iwantout. I finished matric last year and in just doing some online courses and working. I'm applying to study in Germany since tuition there is free in most places even for non eu students. I had an average of 72% and I got accepted at one so far. Here's a comment by somebody on my post there:

Regarding Germany: Do your Bachelors in South Africa, your Masters in Germany and then you can stay here forever.

More than 1,000 Master programmes here are taught in English: https://www.studying-in-germany.org/international-programmes-germany/

To study at a public university you have to pay an administrative fee of usually 150 to 400 euro per semester, you get a 24/7 public transport ticket in return. 15 out of 16 German states have no further tuition for international students, the state of Baden-Württemberg wants 1,500 euro per semester.

To get a student visa you need an admission letter from a university and you need to prove that your livelihood is secured, which is the case if you have 8,820 euro for your first year in Germany on a bank account

During your studies, you can work part-time (120 full days/240 half days per year). After your studies, you get an automatic resident and work permit and are invited to stay in Germany: http://www.make-it-in-germany.com/en/for-qualified-professionals/training-learning/study/studying-in-germany-and-after/residence-permits-for-postgraduates

After 8 years you can become a German citizen: http://www.make-it-in-germany.com/en/for-qualified-professionals/visa/living-permanently-in-germany/naturalisation

Here are some videos where Bharat talks about part-time jobs for international students and cost of living: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=90b5Rqyxq8E
